title: 2026-11-05_Mirai_Botnet_Investigation_841
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a compromised network infected with the Mirai botnet. Your goal is to identify and contain the malicious activities, including C2 communication, data collection, and flood attacks.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a compromised network infected with the Mirai botnet. Your goal is to identify and contain the malicious activities, including C2 communication, data collection, and flood attacks.

levels.title: Identify the Beacon Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for sending beacon periodically to the C2 Server.
levels.solution: 1. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running` to list all running services. 2. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names. 3. Use the command `systemctl status <service_name>` to get detailed information about the suspicious service. 4. The service responsible for sending beacon periodically to the C2 Server is likely to have a name related to 'beacon' or 'health check'. 5. Use the command `systemctl cat <service_name>` to inspect the service definition and confirm its behavior.

levels.title: Determine the Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution: 1. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services. 2. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names. 3. Use the command `systemctl cat <service_name>` to inspect the service definition. 4. Pay particular attention to the `ExecStart` line, which specifies the path of the script launched by the service. 5. Navigate to the script path specified in the `ExecStart` line. 6. Use a text editor or `cat` command to view the script and identify the communication port with the C2 server.

levels.title: Identify the Scheduling Mechanism
levels.content: Investigators suspect that the C2 beacon service automatically resumes after the system starts and continues to execute periodically. Determine which system component is responsible for scheduling this activity.
levels.solution: 1. Use the command `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers. 2. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious timer names. 3. Use the command `systemctl cat <timer_name>` to inspect the timer definition. 4. Pay particular attention to the `OnCalendar` line, which specifies the schedule for the timer. 5. Use the command `systemctl status <timer_name>` to verify the timer status and confirm its behavior.
